title: Rorca Spec-Aligned Feature Assurance SSDLC

acceptanceCriteria: The map displays a navigable requirement-to-acceptance-criterion-to-story-to-control-to-evidence-to-decision chain for the selected feature.
When a row revision or plan identity differs from its source, the map displays stale state and both identities.
For a fixture containing generated narrative, host-observed evidence, and a missing link, the map displays their distinct sources, timestamps, bindings, trust levels, and gap states.
Focused tests pass for complete, missing, stale, and mismatched projection fixtures and fail for false-green relationships.
userStories.description: Add a read-only Feature Assurance Map that projects the current lifecycle plan, requirements, acceptance criteria, implementation stories, controls, evidence records, decisions, and work-package facts into one traceable view. It reports verified, pending, stale, blocked, and unavailable relationships without changing lifecycle state.
userStories.title: Project a revision-bound Feature Assurance Map

acceptanceCriteria: Submitting a candidate missing each required specification revision, plan, commit, tree, diff, or scope identity returns a missing-identity finding naming that field.
The scope evaluator records each changed, required, allowed, forbidden, unexpected, and missing path for the bound work package.
When an evidence or decision subject differs from the candidate, the validator returns a rejected-subject result and excludes it from satisfaction.
Automated fixtures pass for exact matches and fail for missing identity, path drift, forbidden changes, and wrong-subject evidence.
userStories.description: Create canonical identity and scope checks for an assurance candidate. A candidate binds the selected specification revision and lifecycle plan to the implementation commit, source tree, diff, allowed paths, changed paths, test executions, and produced artifacts when present. Broken lineage is an explicit finding, not a recoverable success.
userStories.title: Bind assurance candidates to exact subject and scope

acceptanceCriteria: For a bound change, the compiler emits a stable obligation set with requirement, change kind, component or boundary, expected evidence, and rationale for every applicable check.
Given contrasting requirement, risk, architecture, and change-scope fixtures, the compiler reports selected and excluded checks with a rationale for each.
Given absent or conflicting inputs, the compiler emits explicit not-applicable, unresolved, or blocked dispositions and never emits passing state for a required check.
Focused tests pass for deterministic repeated compilation and fail for changed-boundary, deleted-behavior, scope-drift, and missing-rationale fixtures.
userStories.description: Implement Development Assurance as a deterministic compiler that converts the bound feature, requirements, risks, architecture decisions, and implementation scope into explicit obligations and checks. It reuses current work-package and lifecycle seams rather than creating a parallel governance engine.
userStories.title: Compile Development Assurance obligations from changed work

acceptanceCriteria: Every accepted execution record contains runner, command, start and finish time, exit status, counts, output digest, exact candidate identity, and environment identity.
JUnit XML, Jest or Vitest, and Pytest fixtures return normalized passed, failed, skipped, blocked, quarantined, and malformed outcomes without inventing success.
For an explicit stable test-case-to-obligation mapping, coverage returns satisfied only when a passing execution matches the exact bound candidate.
Zero-test, skipped-only, stale, malformed, wrong-commit, missing-mapping, and failed-execution fixtures return blocked or insufficient coverage.
userStories.description: Add a canonical test-obligation, test-case, execution, result, and coverage model fed by real runner output. Start with JUnit XML plus Jest or Vitest and Pytest result adapters; retain exact execution provenance and evaluate coverage through stable obligation identifiers, not test-name substring guesses.
userStories.title: Normalize real test execution and requirement coverage

acceptanceCriteria: For a bound candidate, the compiler returns the active profile, selected controls, applicability rationale, effective thresholds, and unselected controls.
A test registering a declared workspace extension returns its namespace and additive controls, and rejects an extension that mutates shared core or another workspace.
Absent, invalid, or conflicting profile fixtures return unresolved or blocked controls and a corrective action rather than a default passing state.
Tests pass for deterministic selection, extension isolation, conflict reporting, baseline preservation, and exact repeatability.
userStories.description: Provide deterministic, versioned assurance profiles that refine common controls for a workspace without modifying Rorca core contracts. Profile selection is based on the bound product, requirements, risks, architecture, and change scope; extensions remain namespaced, inspectable, and unable to erase required baseline controls.
userStories.title: Compile proportionate assurance profiles with workspace extensions

acceptanceCriteria: Standards and Design review fixtures return independently attributable findings that identify the bounded subject and reviewed source locations.

Adversarial fixtures for story-pass-without-tests, stale replay, wrong-subject evidence, fake output, weakened assertions, missing negative coverage, and scope expansion return named detections or bounded unresolved findings.
The review view displays independent, self-review, and stale-review trust states, and returns insufficient evidence when independent review is required but unavailable.
Regression fixtures for reproducible assurance incidents return their expected detection outcome.
userStories.description: Add independent Standards, Design, and adversarial review axes for feature assurance work. Each reviewer receives a bounded subject and returns structured findings with exact source locations, severity, disposition, freshness, and reviewer provenance. Results are evidence for inspection, never self-issued approval.
userStories.title: Evaluate isolated review axes and adversarial assurance cases

acceptanceCriteria: The dogfood path emits an AssuredCandidate containing bound feature, plan, candidate, obligations, evidence links, evaluation outcomes, unresolved findings, and freshness data.
When an obligation is missing, stale, rejected, or insufficient, the handoff records that condition and returns a non-all-satisfied outcome.
Replay, restart, and partial-failure fixtures preserve immutable observations, record the recovery decision, and never promote a partial attempt.
Dogfood output records assurance trends and routes incident observations as governed improvement inputs without changing upstream lifecycle facts.
userStories.description: Dogfood the complete feature-assurance path in Rorca and emit an AssuredCandidate only when the selected candidate has all required bound evidence or explicit unresolved findings. The handoff is a read-only, revision-bound data product for later consumers; it cannot change lifecycle status, merge code, perform production actions, or bypass existing governance.
userStories.title: Dogfood a non-authorizing AssuredCandidate handoff
